items.title: [The Guardian Global Development] Fifty billion trees by 2030: how Ethiopia is recruiting citizens across the country to plant, plant, plant
items.content_html:
After losing much of its forests in recent decades, the country’s people have led the way in planting saplings across the country as part of the government’s Green Legacy Initiative

When Halima Kedir first began planting trees, she was met with scepticism and even mockery. “My neighbours discouraged me,” she recalls, sitting on a wooden chair in her garden, which is lush with the trees and fruits she has planted – banana, olive and grevillea among them.

“They thought I was striving for nothing, but with time, many are realising that trees can be part of the solution to our problems as a way to fight climate change and food insecurity,” she says.

items.content_html:
🌾 🏔️ 🔭 ✏️

🌾 🏔️ 🔭 ✏️

U.S. irrigation produces some greenhouse gas emissions, but new research suggests it prevents vastly more by allowing farmers to grow more food on less land. Without irrigation, replacing lost crop yields could require converting natural ecosystems into farmland, releasing an estimated 6.86 gigatons of greenhouse gases. That is equivalent to about 363 years of current annual U.S. irrigation emissions.

items.title: [Kagi Small Web] oh, right, that’s another way the electricity generation investments motivated by AI can still pay…
items.content_html:
neorealis:

climate change probably isnt gonna turn the earth into venus, it’s gonna kill a few hundred million people in the global south and a few hundred thousand old people in the global north, and your electric bill is going to become expensive enough that you may need to choose between being comfortable and other luxuries if you want to live wherever you want.

but you wont need to care about it. you’ll be able to snark on your 90th birthday about how worried everyone was about it when you were young and how “nothing happened.” nobody much younger than you will be able to conceptualize how the world changed drastically enough to argue with you. the “i told you so” types will all have killed themselves with sustance abuse long ago

oh, right, that’s another way the electricity generation investments motivated by AI can still pay off even if AI power usage doesn’t live up to expectations

🌾 ✏️

🌾 ✏️

Leaders in Pando region denounce opaque deals over carbon credits as government and companies rush to monetise Amazon rainforest after 2024 ruling

In the village plazas of Pando, a remote northern Amazonian region of Bolivia, the main talk is no longer just about the next harvest. One pressing issue is the “invisible air” being sold to foreigners who regularly visit their communities.

In June 2024, the country’s constitutional court struck down the ban on a funding mechanism linked to carbon markets. Since then, Indigenous leaders of three ethnic groups – the Tacana, Ese Ejja and Cabineño – have complained about companies and foundations that arrive with offers of “climate solutions”, often during the ever more frequent droughts or floods.

items.title: [ScienceDaily] Back-to-back Arctic storms can double sea ice loss
items.content_html:
🎨 🪶 🌲 🏔️ 🔭 ✏️

🎨 🪶 🌲 🏔️ 🔭 ✏️

🎨 🪶 🌲 🏔️ 🔭 ✏️

🎨 🪶 🌲 🏔️ 🔭 ✏️

Scientists have found that Arctic cyclones become especially destructive when several strike one after another. These storm clusters cause about twice as much sea ice loss as isolated cyclones, with impacts that persist roughly two and a half times longer. As Arctic ice becomes thinner and weaker, the damage from these storms appears to be increasing, potentially creating a feedback loop that accelerates future ice loss.

items.title: [ScienceDaily] Global warming is breaking a 400-year climate link between two oceans
items.content_html: The Indian and Pacific oceans have been climatically linked for centuries, but scientists say that connection is now breaking down in an exceptional way.
